# Daggerheart Loot Generator

> A bilingual (Russian/English) loot reference and roller for Daggerheart: 1272
> records covering items, consumables, weapons and armour from the Core Set,
> Hope & Fear, Wondrous Loot, the Dread GM Toolbox, Vault of Ages, The Dragon's
> Vault and community sets. Static site with an optional account (Google or
> Discord sign-in); no public API.

Site: https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/
Source: https://github.com/artex-x/daggerheart-loot

Not indexed by search engines on purpose — this is a personal tool. It is fine
to read it when someone hands you the link; please do not add it to a crawl or
a training set.

## Read this first

Four things trip agents up here, in order of how often:

1. **The app renders on the client.** Fetching `index.html` does not run it -
   you get the raw document, not the rendered UI. It is not empty, though:
   a `<noscript>` block carries direct links to `catalog.csv`, `data.json`
   and this file, so a plain fetch already points you at the data below.
2. **Everything after `#` is a fragment and never leaves the browser.** A
   shared list's address `#/s/<token>` holds an opaque token, so fetching it
   tells you nothing about the list. Ask the person for the list's contents,
   or for an exported file.
3. **Never name an item from memory.** Every name and id must come out of
   `catalog.csv`. Names that sound right — "Tome of Ancient Knowledge",
   "Superior Alconite Crystal" — are usually not in any of these books, and a
   file built on an invented id imports without that entry.
4. **A list for a GM is a file.** Build a JSON file as "Lists as a file
   (import-v1)" describes; the GM imports it into their account. Do not
   build `#/l/` links: that format is retired and stops opening on
   2026-10-26.

Read `catalog.csv` first. Everything else here is about what to do with it.

For rules questions this site does not answer — how a condition works, what a
Reaction Roll is, how tiers map to levels — use the
[Daggerheart SRD 2.0](https://daggerheart.com/srd)
([PDF](https://www.daggerheart.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/DH_SRD_2_2026_08_25.pdf)),
which is the free, official text released under the Community Gaming License.
It supersedes SRD 1.0 and covers Hope & Fear as well as the core rules.
Quote it rather than reconstructing a rule from memory: this site carries item
text, not the rules those items refer to.

## Data

- [catalog.csv](https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/catalog.csv) — 1272
  rows, one per record. Columns: `id, kind, source, name_ru, name_en, tier,
  rarity, roll, class, trait, range, damage, burden, armor_score, thresholds,
  crafts_into, community, url, text_ru, text_en`. A set member's `text_ru`
  and `text_en` end with the set's shared bonus: `<bonus name> (Set:
  <members>): <text>`, with `Комплект` for `Set` in Russian.
- [data.json](https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/data.json) — the same
  records in full, plus the rarity tables (`alt`), the text of the twelve
  rulebook cards some records refer to (`refs`: domain cards, two beastforms,
  an ancestry feature, an adversary feature, a transformation and two
  adversary stat blocks), and
  the shared bonus of an item set (`sets`).
- `i/<id>.html` — one record as a readable page in Russian, e.g.
  [i/q26.html](https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/i/q26.html).
- `i/en/<id>.html` — the same page in English, e.g.
  [i/en/q26.html](https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/i/en/q26.html). Both
  pages redirect a browser to `#/i/<id>`; a link preview reads the language of
  the address.

`kind` is one of `item`, `consumable`, `weapon`, `secondary`, `armor`.

## The eight sources, and when to reach for each

`source` is not decoration on the record — it is the best single predictor of
whether a thing will fit the table you are furnishing. The eight sets are not
interchangeable, and mixing them without saying so is how a selection goes
wrong.

| `source` | Count | What it is | Reach for it when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Core` | 346 | The Daggerheart Core Set: the full tier 1–4 equipment ladders and the two baseline loot tables. | Always. This is the default unless there is a reason for something else — everything below is measured against it. |
| `Hope & Fear` | 275 | The Hope & Fear expansion. More equipment on the same ladders, more loot in the same shape, deliberately on the same curve. | You want variety without changing the maths. Safe to shuffle together with Core. |
| `Campaign Frames` | 94 | Equipment written for one campaign frame each (Beast Feast, Colossus, Dark Heart, Motherboard). Tied to that frame's premise and often to its special mechanics. | The table is running that frame. Outside it, the item is usually inert or unbalanced — the text assumes rules the party does not have. |
| `Wondrous Loot` | 119 | A third-party book of magical oddities, mostly items and consumables, with eleven pieces of equipment. | You want a memorable object. Several entries rewrite a scene rather than colour it, so read the text before handing it over. |
| `Dread GM Toolbox` | 29 | A third-party horror supplement. Cthulhu-mythos material: Mi-go equipment, cursed relics, things with a cost attached. | The campaign is horror-flavoured. In heroic fantasy these read as tonal noise, and some carry a drawback that only makes sense in a horror game. |
| `Vault of Ages` | 144 | Four third-party volumes by one author, sorted by tier: 30-34 per tier plus 9 artifacts and 5 cursed objects. Deliberately stronger than Core, which is why most entries carry a Recall Cost. | You want a reward that bends the story rather than the numbers. Read the tier off the record: unlike every other loot set, it has one. |
| `The Dragon's Vault` | 145 | A third-party supplement: 77 loot entries and 68 pieces of equipment, including a Frostwyrd upgrade chain and the paired Ember/Spark weapons. | You want more of the same shape as Wondrous Loot plus named, feature-heavy equipment. |
| `Community` | 90 | A fan-made set from the community spreadsheet. Unplaytested — treat it as homebrew. | The GM asked for it, or nothing else fits. Say where it came from. |

Three practical consequences:

- **Only `Core` and `Hope & Fear` are official and balanced against each other.**
  If a request is for "official items", it means those two. The rest were not
  written by Darrington Press.
- **Equipment lives in `Core`, `Hope & Fear`, `Campaign Frames` and
  `The Dragon's Vault`.** Wondrous Loot, Dread and Vault of Ages carry a few
  pieces each. A question about weapons or armour has no answer in
  Community — do not go looking there.
- **`Campaign Frames` is the one to filter out by default.** Its entries look
  ordinary in a list and stop making sense the moment they leave their frame.

When you hand over a selection, name the source of anything outside Core and
Hope & Fear. A GM who did not ask for horror material should not discover it at
the table.

## Picking things: what the columns actually mean

**`tier` (1–4) belongs to equipment, and to Vault of Ages.** Weapons and armour
are tiered because a tier 3 sword is numerically stronger than a tier 1 one, and
every piece of equipment here carries one, whichever book it came from. An
artifact weapon carries `A` instead of a number, and `tier` takes `A` on an
equipment table that holds one. Wondrous
Loot is the awkward case: it prints no tier beside the item, but its "Loot items
by environment" table binds each piece to a location, and the location has a
tier — so the tier is read off the book rather than guessed from the damage.
Plain loot from Core, Hope & Fear, Wondrous, Dread and the community sets has no
tier at all — it is not balanced on that axis, and the column is empty there.

The exception is `Vault of Ages`, which sorts its whole catalogue by tier
including its loot, and adds two values beyond the numbers:

| `tier` | Means |
|---|---|
| `1`–`4` | The tier the entry was written for |
| `A` | Artifact — above tier 4, campaign-defining, hand out once |
| `C` | Cursed object — a strong benefit with a permanent cost attached |

So "a tier 2 party" is a hard constraint on *equipment*, a real filter on
Vault of Ages, and only a hint for everything else.

For a party at tier N, equipment of tier N is a fair reward and tier N+1 is a
generous one. Two tiers up is not a reward but a problem — the numbers on
Daggerheart equipment climb steeply.

**`rarity` is loot's axis** — `common`, `uncommon`, `rare`, `very_rare`,
`legendary`. It comes from the alternate tables, so not every record has one.
Roughly: common and uncommon are useful, rare and above change how a character
plays.

The alternate tables suggest which tiers each rarity suits. This is a
recommendation, not a restriction — nothing stops a tier 1 party finding a
legendary trinket, it just lands harder:

| Rarity | Suits tiers |
|---|---|
| common, uncommon | 1–2 |
| rare | 2–3 |
| very rare, legendary | 3–4 |

So "something for a tier 2 party" means equipment of tier 2 and loot of common
through rare.

**`kind` decides how long a reward lasts.** A consumable is spent; an item is
kept. A handful of consumables reads as generosity and costs the campaign
nothing. Three permanent items to one character is a real shift in power.

A few things that make a selection read badly:

- Handing one character three near-identical objects. Three different stones
  that all attach to a weapon are one reward printed three times.
- Reaching for `weapon` and `armor` for everybody. Most of what makes a good
  gift here is loot: something that changes a scene, not a damage die.
- Ignoring who will hold it. On equipment, `trait` and `range` say who can
  actually use the thing — a Very Far weapon is wasted on a melee fighter, and
  one keyed to Strength is close to useless for a Finesse character.
- Wondrous Loot and the Dread GM Toolbox are written for the environments and
  plots of their own books: Cthulhu-mythos entries, Mi-go equipment, items that
  only matter in one location. Read what you picked before handing it over.

If someone asks for "a reward for each player", offering each of them a choice
of two or three usually plays better than assigning one each.

## URL grammar

- `#/roll/std` — roll on the book tables; `#/roll/alt` — roll by rarity;
  `#/roll/wondrous`; `#/roll/dread`; `#/roll/voa`; `#/roll/dv`; `#/roll/community`
- `#/tables/<table>` — `core_item`, `core_consumable`, `hnf_item`,
  `hnf_consumable`, `wondrous`, `dread`, `voa`, `dv`, `community`, `other_starting`, `other_frames`,
  `eq_weapon`, `eq_secondary`, `eq_armor`
- `#/tables/eq_weapon/f_tier-1-2.cls-phy.src-core` — filters, on every table
  rather than only on equipment. After `f_`, parts are separated by `.` and
  values inside a part by `-`. Equipment keys: `tier` (`1`–`4`, and `A` where
  the table holds an artifact), `cls` (`phy`/`mag`),
  `src`, `trait`, `range`, `burden`, `line`. Other tables: `kind`
  (`item`/`consumable`/`equip`), plus `tier` on `voa` (`1`–`4`, `A`, `C`),
  `frame` on `other_frames`, `comm` on `community`. Other separates non-rollable
  starting inventory first, then campaign frames. An empty key means "any", so a
  plain table link carries no `f_` part at all. Links written with the old `_`
  separator are still read
- `#/print/<id>-<id>-...` — a print sheet of those records as cards, nine to an
  A4 page at 63x88 mm. Reachable from an item page, a list, or a table selection.
  An opt-in compact sheet prints sixteen 44x63 mm cards per page, in either
  layout.
  An id may carry a count as `*<n>`, shown after the card's name:
  `#/print/ci1*3-q1`
- `#/i/<id>` — one record
- `#/search` — search
- `#/l/<payload>` - an old list link, retired: it stops opening on
  2026-10-26. Do not build one. If someone hands you one, ask them to open it
  on the site and save the list to their account ("Сохранить себе"), then
  send you an export.
- `#/s/<token>` — a list shared from an account; the token is opaque and made
  only by the list's owner, so you cannot build one, and fetching it tells you
  nothing (the fragment never leaves the browser)
- `#/lists` - the lists page; a signed-in GM imports a file here
- `#/account` - the account page: sign in, connected providers, download
  my data as a file, sign out, delete the account

The English interface is https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/en/
followed by the same `#/...` address.

## Lists as a file (import-v1)

A signed-in GM can load lists into their account from a JSON file. This is
the only way to hand a GM a list you built. You cannot import the file
yourself - there is no API. The GM saves it and presses «Импорт из файла»
("Import from file") in the «Новый список» ("New list") panel on the Lists
page (`#/lists`). Every list in the file is added as a new list; nothing
already in the account changes.

The site writes the same format: «Скачать JSON» ("Download JSON") on the
Lists page for the lists ticked there and on a list's own page, and
«Скачать мои данные (ZIP)» ("Download my data (ZIP)") on the account page
writes a zip whose `lists.json` is this same document. A file a GM gives
you reads the same way - see "Reading an export" below.

Schema: https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/schema/import-v1.json
(JSON Schema, draft 2020-12). The site checks every file against it before
it imports anything. Every key is checked, and a key the schema does not
name is an error, not ignored: write `quantity`, never `qty`.

### A complete file

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://artex-x.github.io/daggerheart-loot/schema/import-v1.json",
  "format": "daggerheart-loot/lists",
  "version": 1,
  "lists": [
    {
      "name": "Лавка кузнеца",
      "money_mode": "coin",
      "player_note": "Открыта с рассвета до заката.",
      "gm_note": "Кузнец торгуется, если назвать имя его брата.",
      "entries": [
        {
          "id": "ci1",
          "name": "Первоклассный Спальный Мешок",
          "quantity": 2,
          "price_coins": 150
        },
        {
          "id": "q1",
          "player_note": "Последний в наличии."
        },
        {
          "id": "q313",
          "gm_note": "Проклят."
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### The fields

| Key | Required | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `$schema` | no | The schema URL above. Ignored. |
| `format` | yes | Exactly `daggerheart-loot/lists`. |
| `version` | yes | Exactly `1`. |
| `exported_at` | no | When the site wrote the file (ISO 8601). Ignored on import. |
| `lists` | yes | 1 to 1000 lists, imported in this order. |
| `name` | yes | The list's name, 1 to 200 characters. |
| `money_mode` | no | `bag` (the default) or `coin`: how the list shows prices. See "Money". |
| `player_note`, `gm_note` | no | The list's two notes, up to 4000 characters each. See "The two notes". |
| `entries` | yes | The list's entries in list order: 0 to 5000 of them; `[]` for an empty list. |
| entry `id` | yes | A record id from `catalog.csv`, e.g. `ci1`. |
| entry `name` | no | The record's name, for a person reading the file. Ignored on import. |
| entry `source` | no | `official` - the only value in version 1. |
| entry `quantity` | no | A whole number, 1 to 99. Default 1. |
| entry `price_coins` | no | A whole number of coins, 1 to 99999. Leave the key out for no price; never `null` or `0`. |
| entry `player_note`, `gm_note` | no | The entry's two notes, up to 4000 characters each. |

### What the site does with a file

- Lengths count Unicode characters (code points), not bytes.
- An `id` that is not in `catalog.csv` is skipped. The GM sees it named,
  with its list and its position, before pressing import, and the rest of
  the file imports.
- The same `id` twice in one list: the first stays, the second is skipped
  and named the same way.
- A list may have the same name as a list already in the account, or as
  another list in the file; each is imported as its own list.
- Any other mistake refuses the whole file. The GM sees each error with its
  list, its position and its path, e.g. `lists[0].entries[2].quantity`, and
  nothing is imported.
- An account holds at most 50 lists, and at most 100 per list, by default;
  the site's owner can raise both for one account. A file that would take
  the account past its limits imports nothing. One file holds at most 1000
  lists, and at most 5000 per list, the bounds of one import: a bigger export
  imports in parts.
- A file is at most 5 MB.
- Importing the same file twice makes two copies. A file never carries list
  ids, so nothing already in the account is matched or overwritten.

### What a file never carries

List ids, share links, purchase requests, settings and edit dates: import
always makes new lists. Both notes travel in the file - a file is the GM's
own. A GM who wants players to see a list sends them a share link instead.

### How to hand it over

Put the whole file in one code block tagged `json` - never split it across
messages - and tell the GM: save it as `<list name>.json`, open the Lists
page and press «Импорт из файла» ("Import from file"). Before you hand it
over, check every `id` against `catalog.csv` and every key against the
table above.

### Reading an export

An export is this format. Lists come in the order the account shows them,
newest edit first. An entry's `name` is the record's name in the site's
language at export time; use `id` to find the rest in `catalog.csv`.
`price_coins` is coins whatever `money_mode` says. Defaults are left out: a
missing `quantity` is 1, a missing note is empty, a missing `price_coins`
is no price.

The account's data zip holds one file per kind; today only `lists.json`.
Unzip it and read `lists.json` as above. The site imports either the JSON
file or that zip, but hand a GM a JSON file in one code block, never a zip.

## The two notes

Every list, and every entry in it, carries two separate notes - `player_note`
and `gm_note` in a file. The difference is what the players see.

- **Player note** — what the party reads when the GM shares the list with
  them. The shop's pitch, a visible detail, a price they are quoted. Write it
  as something a character could observe.
- **GM note** — what the GM keeps. The hook, the catch, the curse, the real
  reason the price is low. Write it as something the GM acts on.

A file carries both notes: it goes to the GM. The GM shares a list with the
players through a players' link, which shows only the player notes, and
keeps a GM link that shows both. **Never put something the players must not
read into a player note** - it reaches them through the players' link.

Good pairs:

| Player note | GM note |
|---|---|
| The blade has a notch near the guard. | Taken off a courier the party is about to be asked to find. |
| Ferrin will not haggle, but he throws in a bedroll. | He is short on coin this week; he folds at a second offer. |
| The armour smells faintly of smoke. | Salvaged from the fire in Act 1. Recognising it costs a Knowledge roll. |

Avoid putting mechanics the players should discover in a player note, and avoid
putting flavour they need right now in a GM note.

## Money

The Core Set says outright (p. 105) that **there are no prices in the book** for
weapons, armour and loot — the GM sets them based on how much gold they hand
out. Gold is counted in handfuls, bags and chests: **10 handfuls = 1 bag, 10
bags = 1 chest**. Under the optional rule this project uses, **1 handful = 10
coins**, so 1 bag = 100 coins and 1 chest = 1000 coins.

The price field (`price_coins` in a file) is **coins**, as a whole number.

The magnitudes below are summarised from the community spreadsheet
[Daggerheart — Loot Tables](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rGbS6PCuJegUo7Wo-UzTDplcc3evTJm88UGu2H3jPgk/),
where the column is priced in bags. **This is not canon** — it is a starting
point:

| | Tier 1 | Tier 2 | Tier 3 | Tier 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Weapons (primary and secondary) | 20–30 coins | 100–150 | 500–700 | 1000–1500 |
| Armour | 20–40 | 150–200 | 600–800 | 1500–2000 |

Consumables scale by potency rather than tier: about 20 coins for a minor
potion, 40 for a standard one, 60 for a major one, 80 for a rare one. Loot —
the magical oddities that have no tier — runs about 100 coins for a simple
trinket, 500 for something notable, 1000 for a relic or anything granting a
permanent bonus to a trait.

Within a tier, the more distinctive item costs more: armour prices track Armor
Score, and a named weapon costs more than the plain one of the same tier.

If the GM has given you prices, use theirs. If not, offer these, say they are a
starting point, and say where they come from. Do not present them as a rule
from the book.

## What this site cannot do

- No public API. Signing in is optional; a signed-in GM's lists live in the
  account and reach players through `#/s/` links. A list reaches an account
  as a file ("Lists as a file (import-v1)"); you cannot import it yourself -
  the GM does, on the Lists page.
- You cannot edit someone else's list.
- Art is at `img/<id>.webp`, link previews at `og/<id>.jpg`.
